meta.title: Health Indicators Research: Phase 1
meta.reviewStatus: draft - sources being verified (re-check vs NASA resources on Nov 13)
meta.howToEvaluate: For the latest value: if any 'urgent' condition is true (and, when consecutiveDays > 1, it was true for that many days in a row ending today) -> red. Else if all 'normal' conditions are true -> green. Otherwise -> yellow. Never hardcode these numbers in code.
meta.howOftenNote: 'howOften' is the team's suggested routine for the app, not a NASA schedule.
meta.disclaimer: Decision support only, not a medical diagnosis.

indicators.name: Resting heart rate
indicators.basis: NEWS2 bands (score 0 = green, 1-2 = yellow, 3 = red). MedlinePlus normal resting = 60-100.
indicators.whyItMatters: Weightlessness changes blood circulation and how the heart works.

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: NEWS2 Chart 1
NASA HRP: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations

measurement.equipment: Heart rate monitor; CSA Bio-Monitor shirt
measurement.whyNeeded: Microgravity changes how the heart and blood vessels work.
measurement.howToMeasure: Sit still 5 min after waking. Count pulse at wrist for 30 s and x2, or read the heart rate monitor.

source.name: NASA NTRS: Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) report

indicators.name: Blood pressure - systolic (top number)
indicators.basis: Low side: NEWS2 (<=90 = score 3). High side: American Heart Association (120+ elevated, >180 = hypertensive crisis).
indicators.whyItMatters: After spaceflight the body struggles to hold blood pressure on standing.

sources.name: American Heart Association: Understanding Blood Pressure Readings
Royal College of Physicians: NEWS2 Chart 1

measurement.equipment: Blood pressure cuff (ISS Medical Diagnostics Pack, CHeCS)
measurement.whyNeeded: Fluid shifts in space; on return, blood pressure can drop on standing.
measurement.howToMeasure: Sit, rest 5 min, arm at heart level, cuff on bare upper arm. Take 2 readings 1 min apart and use the average.

source.name: NASA NTRS: Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) report

indicators.name: Blood pressure - diastolic (bottom number)
indicators.basis: American Heart Association (80+ = stage 1, >120 = crisis). MedlinePlus normal from 60.

sources.name: American Heart Association: Understanding Blood Pressure Readings
NIH MedlinePlus: Vital signs

measurement.equipment: Blood pressure cuff (ISS Medical Diagnostics Pack, CHeCS)
measurement.whyNeeded: Fluid shifts in space; on return, blood pressure can drop on standing.
measurement.howToMeasure: Sit, rest 5 min, arm at heart level, cuff on bare upper arm. Take 2 readings 1 min apart and use the average.

source.name: NASA NTRS: Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) report

openItems: GAP in research: no range is given for diastolic below 60. Fallback used: warning (yellow). Ask Eman to confirm.

indicators.name: Breathing rate
indicators.whyItMatters: Early sign of low oxygen or high cabin CO2.

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: NEWS2 Chart 1
NASA HRP: Risk of Hypoxia

measurement.whyNeeded: Early sign of low oxygen or high cabin CO2.
measurement.howToMeasure: Count breaths for 30 s while relaxed and x2. Don't change your breathing while counting.

indicators.name: Blood oxygen (SpO2), on air
indicators.whyItMatters: Spacewalk preparation can raise the risk of mild hypoxia.

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: NEWS2 Chart 1
NASA HRP: Risk of Hypoxia

measurement.whyNeeded: Detects low oxygen (hypoxia), e.g. around spacewalks.
measurement.howToMeasure: Clip pulse oximeter on a warm finger, stay still 30-60 s, read the steady number.

indicators.name: Body temperature
indicators.basis: NEWS2 bands (39.1+ scores 2 in NEWS2; team marks it red). MedlinePlus normal = 36.5-37.3.
indicators.whyItMatters: The immune system weakens in space; fever can be the first infection sign.

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: NEWS2 Chart 1
NASA HRP: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses

measurement.whyNeeded: Immune system weakens in space; fever = possible infection.
measurement.howToMeasure: Measure under the tongue, mouth closed, no drink for 15 min before.

indicators.name: Fasting blood sugar
indicators.basis: CDC: normal <=99, prediabetes 100-125, diabetes >=126; low <70, severe low <54. Red here = contact flight surgeon, not always an emergency.
indicators.whyItMatters: Diet and activity change on long missions. Note: not a routine daily astronaut test; team to decide whether to keep it.

sources.name: CDC: Diabetes Testing
CDC: Low Blood Sugar (Hypoglycemia)

measurement.whyNeeded: Diet and activity change on long missions.
measurement.howToMeasure: Before breakfast after 8+ h without food. Finger prick, glucose meter.
measurement.howOften: Weekly or as planned by team

indicators.decisionNote: DECISION NEEDED (research doc): keep fasting blood sugar? Astronauts do not test it daily. Implemented as an OPTIONAL indicator (not required for a completed check-in).

indicators.name: Sleep last night

text.urgent: less than 6 for 3 nights in a row

indicators.basis: CDC: healthy adult sleep = 7+ h. NASA schedules 8.5 h; astronauts averaged ~6 h (NASA-funded Lancet study). The 3-night red rule is a TEAM CHOICE, not a medical standard.
indicators.whyItMatters: Light-dark cycle is broken (16 sunrises a day on ISS); poor sleep hurts performance.

sources.name: CDC: 1 in 3 adults don't get enough sleep
NASA HRP: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules

measurement.equipment: Actigraphy watch (used in NASA Standard Measures)
measurement.whyNeeded: 16 sunrises a day on ISS disturb sleep; poor sleep hurts performance.
measurement.howToMeasure: Enter hours slept. On ISS a wrist actigraphy watch records sleep.

indicators.teamChoiceNote: TEAM CHOICE: design decision of the team, not a medical standard. Needs approval. (3-night red rule).
openItems: GAP in research: a single night under 6 h is not defined. Fallback used: warning (yellow); red only after 3 nights in a row.

indicators.name: Cabin CO2 (1-hour average)
indicators.basis: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 [V2 6004] limit = 3 mmHg (1-hr avg). OCHMO TB-004: headaches reported 2.8-4.5 mmHg; fatigue, poor sleep, nausea above 4.5.
indicators.whyItMatters: CO2 builds up inside a closed spacecraft.

sources.name: NASA OCHMO: Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004: Carbon Dioxide
NASA OCHMO: Human Spaceflight Standards + Technical Briefs

measurement.whyNeeded: CO2 builds up in a closed cabin and causes headaches.
measurement.howToMeasure: Read from spacecraft environment sensor (not a body measurement). Watch for headache.

source.name: NASA OCHMO: Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004: Carbon Dioxide

indicators.name: Radiation dose - career total
indicators.basis: NASA limit: career < 600 mSv (red). 300 mSv (= 50% of limit) yellow line is a TEAM CHOICE. Separate alert: one solar particle event limited to 250 mSv.
indicators.whyItMatters: Space radiation raises cancer risk; outside Earth's magnetic field it is much higher.

sources.name: NASA OCHMO: Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020: Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection
NASA Human Research Program: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight

measurement.whyNeeded: Space radiation raises cancer risk; NASA sets a career limit.
measurement.howToMeasure: Read personal dosimeter; app adds today's dose to the running total.

source.name: NASA OCHMO: Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020: Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection

indicators.teamChoiceNote: TEAM CHOICE: design decision of the team, not a medical standard. Needs approval. (300 mSv yellow line = 50% of the limit).

extraRule.description: A single solar particle event is limited to 250 mSv (NASA OCHMO TB-020).
extraRule.appliesTo: dose from a single solar particle event
extraRule.level: not specified in research - to be confirmed

source.name: NASA OCHMO: Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020: Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection

openItems: Career total = dose from earlier missions + sum of daily doses entered. Research does not say how to get the starting value: app uses a profile field defaulting to 0.

indicators.name: Exercise today

text.urgent: less than 60 for 2 days in a row

indicators.basis: JAXA: ISS crew exercise 2 hours a day. Yellow/red cut-offs are a TEAM CHOICE.
indicators.whyItMatters: Bones lose about 1-2% mass per month in microgravity; exercise slows it.

sources.name: JAXA: Bisphosphonates as a Countermeasure to Bone Loss
NASA NTRS: Digital Astronaut Project Bone Remodeling Model

measurement.whyNeeded: Without gravity bones lose 1-2%; exercise slows it.
measurement.howToMeasure: Enter minutes on treadmill, bike and resistance device.

source.name: JAXA: Bisphosphonates as a Countermeasure to Bone Loss

indicators.teamChoiceNote: TEAM CHOICE: design decision of the team, not a medical standard. Needs approval. (yellow and red cut-offs).
openItems: GAP in research: a single day under 60 min is not defined. Fallback used: warning (yellow); red only after 2 days in a row.

indicators.name: Mood / stress self-check
indicators.basis: TEAM CHOICE scale (not a clinical test). Linked to NASA behavioral health risk.
indicators.whyItMatters: Isolation and distance from Earth affect mental health.

sources.name: NASA HRP: Risk of Behavioral Conditions and Psychiatric Disorders
NASA Human Research Program: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight

measurement.whyNeeded: Isolation and confinement affect mental health.
measurement.howToMeasure: Answer: 'How do you feel today?' 1-5. Optional note.

source.name: NASA HRP: Risk of Behavioral Conditions and Psychiatric Disorders

indicators.teamChoiceNote: TEAM CHOICE: design decision of the team, not a medical standard. Needs approval. (scale and cut-offs).
openItems: GAP in research: a single day with score 1-2 is not defined. Fallback used: warning (yellow); red only after 2 days in a row.
